answer: Cut the epoch pool into a terrace of fixed steps, then let an agent claim one only through a signal it cannot share: a fingerprint of how it worked, not of what it produced. Agents whose fingerprints cluster together share a single step and split it. A farm of N clones thus collects what one head would, while paying N times the compute, so splitting defeats itself; pooling cannot rescue it, because the divisor follows the cluster, not the owner. Separate neighbors keep separate steps, and the haven of established peers supplies the frame each fingerprint is measured against.
